summary: TLS uploads to private deployment stall on office Wi-Fi after AP firmware update — MTU/PMTU interaction with WireGuard overlay
description:
Issue summary: After an AP firmware push to office Wi-Fi (Cisco 9800 series), a subset of laptops experience TLS upload stalls when sending large payloads to Redwood Private endpoints over WireGuard. Impact: Engineers on-prem cannot push large model bundles or uploads to the private deployment; operations and customer-facing work slowed. Intermittent: small requests succeed; large uploads stall during TLS handshake or mid-upload and eventually time out. Behavior began ~2026-03-09 22:00 PDT shortly after the AP firmware rollout.

Impact: Several internal deploys to the Private cluster in us-west failed; developer productivity affected. No public customer impact reported yet (private deployments only).

Observed behavior:
- Uploads of tar.gz > 1.4 MB hang during TLS handshake or during the first data packets after handshake.
- Application-level logs show stalled HTTP/2 streams and long tail latency on token pushes.
- WireGuard tunnel remains UP per wg show; control plane reports no peer downtime.
- ICMP Fragmentation-needed messages were being dropped by the office edge firewall, but only after the AP firmware change.

Additional notes: This looks like a PMTU/MTU interaction between 802.11ax A-MSDU aggregation, the AP's new fragmentation behavior, and the WireGuard overlay which increases packet size by ~80 bytes (UDP + WG headers).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect to corporate-ssid on affected AP cluster (office floor 4).
2) Establish WireGuard tunnel to private deployment (wg0 to gateway 10.10.0.1).
4) Observe TLS handshake stalls or stall during first POST packet exchange for payloads > ~1300 bytes.
5) Running tcpdump on client shows initial SYN/SYN-ACK, TLS ClientHello, then no progress; server logs show half-open TLS session.
logs:
tcpdump excerpt (client):
14:12:03.123456 IP client > gateway: UDP, length 1420
14:12:03.123789 IP client > 1.2.3.4: TCP 52344 > 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
14:12:03.124012 IP 1.2.3.4 > client: TCP 443 > 52344: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:12:03.124200 IP client > 1.2.3.4: TCP 52344 > 443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1381, ack 1, win 64240, length 1380
14:12:03.124500 IP 1.2.3.4 > client: ICMP 1/4 Fragmentation needed and DF set (mtu = 1350)

Edge firewall (ASA) logs: "Unable to deliver ICMP dest-unreachable frag-needed to host 10.24.12.45, policy drop".

Application log (uploader): "http2 stream stalled: no DATA frames received after ClientHello; retrying; attempt 3 failed: i/o timeout"
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Support triage: Confirmed multiple reports from floor 3/4 seating areas. New AP firmware v17.4.2 pushed 2026-03-09 21:55; rollback window open until 2026-03-12.
2026-03-10 10:10 - SRE checked WireGuard; peers show steady handshake counters and no rekey storms. No packet drops visible on wg endpoints in cloud.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Network Eng performed controlled repro with a MacBook: success when client MTU forced to 1350 locally; failure at default 1500. Suggests PMTU path discovery failing to propagate.

2026-03-10 12:20 - Packet captures on AP showed A-MSDU aggregation creating frames that exceed downstream MTU after WireGuard encapsulation. AP firmware changes now appear to allow larger aggregated frames without honoring DF heuristics; combined with edge firewall ICMP filtering, clients never learn lower MTU.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Tested temporary mitigations: enforced MSS clamping on office edge (ASA) for TCP sessions to 1330; this restores upload success for affected clients. Also validated forcing client MTU to 1350 works around issue.

2026-03-11 11:00 - Cross-team sync: Wireless team confirmed firmware change adjusted aggregation thresholds for HE frames; vendor acknowledged a regression and provided beta patch to disable aggressive aggregation per SSID.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Engineering created a short-term policy to enable MSS clamping on edge for user VLANs and disabled A-MSDU aggregation on corporate-ssid via AP config.
comments: John Miller (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed several deploys failing with 'http2 stream stalled' errors. Happens only on office Wi-Fi; home tethering works fine.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10: Triaged and escalated to Networking. Collected failed pcap and sample client config.
Network Eng (Miguel Ortega) - 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally. Suspect PMTU discovery not propagating due to ICMP filtering + AP aggregation increase. Will test MSS clamp as workaround.
SRE (Sophie Chen) - 2026-03-11: Deployed MSS clamping on edge and requested Wireless to push a config to disable A-MSDU on corp SSID. Noted upload flows recovered for test clients.

Wireless Vendor Rep (Cisco) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed firmware regression in v17.4.2 affecting A-MSDU behavior with overlay tunnels. Beta patch available to toggle behavior; scheduling controlled rollout.
Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-12: Notified impacted engineers of workaround (use wired or set MTU 1350) and tracking permanent fix with Networking.
Sophie Chen - 2026-03-12: Leaving ticket open while vendor rollbacks/patches are validated. Plan: roll back AP firmware on non-critical APs Thu 2026-03-12 window; full fix requires vendor patch.
root_cause: AP firmware v17.4.2 changed 802.11ax A-MSDU aggregation thresholds such that aggregated frames after WireGuard UDP encapsulation exceeded downstream MTU. Edge firewall was configured to drop outgoing ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages to internal hosts, preventing PMTU discovery. Result: TCP MSS not adjusted, causing TLS/data packets to be dropped and uploads to stall.
resolution:
Short-term mitigations applied: 1) MSS clamping (1330) on office edge for user VLANs; 2) Disabled A-MSDU aggregation on corporate-ssid; 3) Guidance to staff: use wired network or set MTU 1350 on client if experiencing issues. Vendor provided beta patch to correct aggregation behavior.

Planned long-term fix: Vendor patch scheduled for controlled rollout week of 2026-03-15 after validation. Post-deployment: remove MSS clamp and re-enable optimized aggregation. Follow-up: add test to CI that repros large TLS upload over WireGuard overlay in office environment to catch regressions.
